requirements.evidence: Every route in the contract is present with the right names and middleware (routes/web.php:20-57, including 'throttle:6,1' on password.email and ['signed','throttle:6,1'] on verification.verify). Login: 'email:strict', a throttle key of lowercase email + IP with 5 tries, auth.failed and auth.throttle errors on email, session()->regenerate() and redirectIntended(route('home')) (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:16-90). Register: Password::defaults(), a 'confirmed' rule, the throttle key Str::transliterate('register|'.ip), Registered, login and regenerate (app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:24-83). Password defaults are configured once (AppServiceProvider.php:24-27). Reset rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset (NewPasswordController.php:36-43). Forgot-password always flashes passwords.sent (PasswordResetLinkController.php:24-27). User implements MustVerifyEmail. The resend action returns verified users to home. .env.example and phpunit.xml pin the locale, lang/{en,pt_BR}/ui.php exist, and the existing welcome and bulma-test views now use route() and translations.

conventions.evidence: Login uses #[Validate] with $this->validate(), but Register declares no #[Validate] attributes and uses a rules() method instead (Register.php:59-67). The conventions name #[Validate] as the project pattern. The controllers validate inline, which matches the 1-2 field guidance. CHANGELOG is updated under [Unreleased]. Inputs use plain wire:model, and links and redirects use route()/redirectRoute. The label/input/@error field block is copy-pasted about 10 times across 5 views (e.g. login.blade.php:31-47, register.blade.php:8-80, reset-password.blade.php:12-60) instead of being extracted into an anonymous Blade component as the conventions ask.

security.evidence: Login is rate limited, and Register is rate limited before validation runs. Sessions are regenerated on login and register, and logout invalidates the session and regenerates the token (LogoutController.php:13-16). The forgot-password response does not reveal whether an account exists. Verification goes through EmailVerificationRequest, which is signed and only verifies the logged-in user. Output is escaped with {{ }}, and $fillable is set on User. Weak point: Login::attemptAuthentication (Login.php:55-73) adds a second lookup, whereRaw('LOWER(email) = ?'), plus Hash::check whenever Auth::attempt fails. That doubles the hashing work on failed logins and adds a custom credential path that diverges from the guard.

tests.evidence: Six feature test files cover login (pt-BR text, success with session regeneration, auth.failed, the 5-try limit, redirect away from login when authenticated), registration (confirmed, default password rule, unique email, IP limiter, VerifyEmail sent), the password reset flow (single email input, rotated remember_token, PasswordReset event, the 429 on the 7th request, unknown email), verification (a tampered id returns 403 and verifies nobody, resend, a verified user is sent home, throttle), and localization (en has no pt-BR strings, a scan for hardcoded hrefs). Gaps: there is no unauthorized-call or tamper test for the Livewire actions (for example an authenticated user calling Login/Register submit), which the policy requires. The throttle tests only assert an error on 'email' and never check the auth.throttle message (LoginTest.php:74-79, RegisterTest.php:112-118).

simplicity.evidence: Both ui.php files define every block twice: top-level keys plus 'auth' => [...] and 'verification' => $verifyEmail aliases (lang/en/ui.php:47-57). Only one alias is used, 'ui.auth.verify_email.sent' (EmailVerificationNotificationController.php:19). The case-insensitive fallback login (Login.php:61-70) is speculative code the task did not ask for. The x-layouts.app component only @includes layouts.app (components/layouts/app.blade.php:1-6), which adds indirection. Form field markup is repeated across views.

readability.evidence: The classes are small and well named (isRateLimited, throttleKey, attemptAuthentication), there is no debug output, and the views are consistent with each other. The aliased translation keys make it unclear which key is canonical: the controller uses ui.auth.verify_email.sent while the view uses ui.verify_email.*.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task, and converting welcome/bulma-test to route() and translations is required by requirements 8-9. Unrequested extras: the Bulma CDN fallback was bumped from 0.9.4 to 1.0.4 (layouts/app.blade.php:15), buttons on the test pages became links to login/register, the config/app.php default name and locale changed, and the case-insensitive login path was added.

issues.explanation: The Livewire security policy requires an unauthorized-call or tamper test for each action, and none exist (e.g. an authenticated user calling Login::submit or Register::submit).
The unrequested case-insensitive fallback runs a raw LOWER(email) query and a second Hash::check after every failed Auth::attempt, which duplicates guard logic and doubles hashing on failed logins.
The 'auth' and 'verification' alias groups duplicate every translation block, and only one aliased key is ever used, which makes the source of truth ambiguous.
Register validates through rules() instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern used in Login.
The Bulma label/input/@error field markup is copy-pasted across five views instead of being extracted into an anonymous Blade component.
The lockout tests only assert that an 'email' error exists, so they would not catch the wrong message being shown instead of auth.throttle.
The Bulma CDN fallback version was bumped from 0.9.4 to 1.0.4, which the task did not ask for.
This component exists only to @include layouts.app, an extra layer of indirection.

review.summary: The change implements the full session auth flow: Livewire login and register with rate limiting, password reset that rotates remember_token, signed e-mail verification, logout, a verified /home, pt-BR-first translations, and route()-only links, with broad feature tests. Requirements and security are handled well. It falls short of approve-as-is because Register does not use the #[Validate] pattern, the Livewire unauthorized-call and tamper tests are missing, the translation keys are duplicated, and the login has an unrequested case-insensitive fallback; these are nits rather than blockers.
